prompt: In a template-driven form, what makes each control?

choices.text: A `FormControl` written in the class
choices.why: That is a reactive form.

choices.text: The `ngModel` directive on each input
choices.why: Right. The `<form>` collects them.

choices.text: The browser, from the input's `name`
choices.why: `name` is the key; `ngModel` makes the control.

choices.text: `FormsModule`, once per form
choices.why: The module provides the directives; each `ngModel` makes one.

prompt: What does `[(ngModel)]="date"` do, with `date` a signal?

choices.text: It copies the signal into the input once, at start
choices.why: It keeps them in step both ways.

choices.text: It keeps the input and the signal in step, both ways
choices.why: Right. Two bindings in one.

choices.text: It fails, because `ngModel` needs a plain field
choices.why: Two-way binding works with a writable signal.

choices.text: It turns the signal into a `FormControl`
choices.why: The control is the directive's own; the signal stays a signal.

prompt: Inside a `<form>`, what does every `ngModel` need?

choices.text: An `id` matching its label
choices.why: That is for the label and a screen reader, not for `ngModel`.

choices.text: A `#ref="ngModel"`
choices.why: A template reference is optional.

choices.text: A `name` attribute
choices.why: Right. Without one it fails at run time.

choices.text: A validator
choices.why: A field may have none.

prompt: How does `min="5"` on an input become a validator?

choices.text: The browser checks it and tells Angular
choices.why: Angular adds `novalidate`; the browser checks nothing.

choices.text: A directive adds `Validators.min(5)`
choices.why: Right. Validation by attribute.

choices.text: It does not; only `required` is read
choices.why: `min` is read too, and the bench showed its message.

choices.text: The class reads the attribute in `ngOnInit`
choices.why: Nothing in the class mentions it.

prompt: Match each template reference with what it gives the template.

pairs.right: the whole form: value, validity, submitted

prompt: Where are the rules of a template-driven form written?

choices.text: In the template, as attributes
choices.why: Right. Which validators, when a message shows, what is sent.

choices.text: In a schema function
choices.why: That is Signal Forms.

choices.text: In validator functions passed to controls
choices.why: That is a reactive form.

choices.text: In the server
choices.why: The server checks again, whatever the form does.

prompt: In `ngAfterViewInit`, the bench's form value was `{}`. Why?

choices.text: The inputs had no values yet
choices.why: An empty value would still be a key; there were no keys.

choices.text: `viewChild` returns an empty form until submit
choices.why: It returned the form; the form had no controls yet.

choices.text: The controls register a moment later
choices.why: Right. A moment later both were there.

choices.text: `ngAfterViewInit` runs before the template
choices.why: It runs after the view is drawn.

prompt: What type is `f.value` in a template-driven form?

choices.text: The type of the class's signals
choices.why: The form does not know about them.

choices.text: `any`
choices.why: Right. Nobody described its shape.

choices.text: `Partial` of the fields, like `form.value` in lesson 14
choices.why: That needs controls declared in code.

choices.text: `string`, because inputs hold text
choices.why: `ngModel` gives numbers for number inputs.

prompt: Why does a cross-field rule such as `distinctDates` cost more in a template-driven form?

choices.text: Template-driven forms cannot have more than one validator per field
choices.why: They can have several.

choices.text: The rule needs the server
choices.why: It is a check of two values in the browser.

choices.text: It must be wrapped in a directive, on an element around the fields
choices.why: Right. A reactive form passes the function to the array.

choices.text: Arrays are not allowed in template-driven forms
choices.why: An `@for` of `ngModel`s works, with generated names.

prompt: Which of these grow harder with the size of a template-driven form? Choose every one.

choices.text: Testing the rules without rendering
choices.why: Right. The form only exists once the template runs.

choices.text: Knowing the type of the value
choices.why: Right. It is `any`.

choices.text: A list of fields whose length changes
choices.why: Right. Generated names in an `@for`.

choices.text: Binding one input to one value
choices.why: That is what it does well.

prompt: In Signal Forms, where does a field's value live?

choices.text: In a `FormControl` the field makes
choices.why: There are no `FormControl`s.

choices.text: In the input element, read on submit
choices.why: The input wrote straight into the model.

choices.text: In the signal you passed to `form()`
choices.why: Right. `model().minutes` changed as the field did.

choices.text: In a service Angular provides
choices.why: Nothing is provided; the model is a field of the class.

prompt: What did `[formField]` write into the page by itself?

choices.text: `aria-describedby`, linking each message
choices.why: That is still yours to write.

choices.text: `required` and `min`
choices.why: Right. The browser's own attributes.

choices.text: The error messages
choices.why: The template drew them, from `errors()`.

choices.text: A `novalidate` on the form
choices.why: That was written by hand.

prompt: Why does the planner not move to Signal Forms now?

choices.text: They cannot validate numbers
choices.why: `min` worked on the minutes.

choices.text: They need zone.js
choices.why: They work zoneless, as the bench did.

choices.text: They are still experimental
choices.why: Right. Reactive forms are stable.

choices.text: They cannot be used beside reactive forms
choices.why: They are designed to be adopted one form at a time.

prompt: A Signal Forms input is bound to its field with `<input [___]="draft.date" />`.
Match each kind of form with where its model is.

pairs.right: a signal of a plain object, with a field tree over it

prompt: Which form suits a newsletter sign-up with one email field?

choices.text: Template-driven is fine
choices.why: Right. One field, no rules across fields, nothing for the class to read.

choices.text: Only Signal Forms, as the newest
choices.why: Newest is not the reason to choose.

choices.text: A reactive `FormArray`
choices.why: There is no list here.

choices.text: None: a single field needs no form
choices.why: A real `<form>` still gives Enter to submit.

prompt: An old template-driven form has grown to thirty fields and three rules across them, and its tests render the page. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Add more directives for the new rules
choices.why: That is the cost growing, not shrinking.

choices.text: Move it to Signal Forms at once, everywhere
choices.why: Experimental, and everywhere is the most expensive way.

choices.text: Rewrite this one form as a reactive form, rules and all
choices.why: Right. Typed values, rules as functions, tests without a template.

choices.text: Leave it, since template-driven forms cannot be changed
choices.why: They can; the question is what keeps paying.
